utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember: where did you see him inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On two occasions I saw him in Hangar Number 6 and the third time I saw him in his office when he called me in for questioning. He wanted to take a statement from me. I know that when I was giving that statement that was some time in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other chance to talk to him while you were in Celebici besides this statement you gave him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only on one occasion, when he was in the Hangar Number 6, when he was pointing some people out that he was going to either release or take to the Musala sports hall. That's the only time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of who was Mr. Mucic's superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally I do not know, but I heard that Zejnil Delalic, whom I only saw once, in Hangar Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. He has just said he had no personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How do you know that Zejnil Delalic was the superior of Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. He just said he had no personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: He said also he saw him inside the camp. Let me ask you: when did you see Zejnil Delalic inside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion Hazim Delic came and said -- and the guards they all said that Zejnil Delalic was coming. On that occasion that was -- there were about four or five armed people surrounding Zejnil Delalic, and on that occasion Hazim Delic was there and I don't know if it was incidentally or -- he fired a bullet that hit the metal railing and it ricocheted and it hit Davor Kuljanin, called Sis, and Davor was taken out after that and he was given some medical help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say approximately when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say from which position inside the hangar could you eyewitness all this? The first one or the second position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Zejnil Delalic and Hazim Delic were there together with other people. Do you know the name of any other people --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- being present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were interrogated by somebody inside the Celebici detention camp. How many times did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice. The first time I was questioned by Mladen Zovko, called Kuhar, and the second time Pavo Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in the camp did these interrogations take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean in the same room in the administration building both times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure of whether that was the same room, but one questioning was on May 24th and the other one was some time in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have any occasion to see which part of the camp was visible from the window of the room where you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could only see Hangar Number 22, what I could see at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you accused of anything specific in those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the two people who interrogated you, the first and second time, in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign any piece of paper after either one of these interrogations or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall that I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they long interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one was; the other one was not. The first one lasted longer than the second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they ask you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, both. The first time and then the second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly they questioned whether I had arms or whether I was arrested with arms, where I was and then where I was from, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am sorry to break into my learned friend's cross-examination. I think it is important we have a clear answer which interrogation produced what questions and what answers; otherwise it is very confusing to ask what would be called in England a "rolled-up" question, in other words about two different interrogations, so we know clearly what was said on each occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually I did understand it to be so. In fact, it is more of a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The question was this: "Well, both. The first time and the second time." In order for clarity to obtain, he must be asked about the first time and then about the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would like the witness to describe the first interrogation and then the second interrogation. What did they ask you in the first interrogation, first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I was already beaten up and when I was giving this statement I only remember that Mladen Zovko, called Kuhar, was there and he questioned me and I remember the questions: whether I had a rifle; whether I had been arrested with a rifle; where I was; whether there was resistance in that area. Those are the only questions I remember from the first questioning. The second questioning was also reduced to where I was from; whether I had a rifle; whether I shot. That is all I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. N, did anybody take your valuables on the occasion of your arrest or during your detention at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. During my stay in Number 22 there was an evening -- I don't know when -- all prisoners who were there who had money, and I had some money, that money was taken away and then also gold watches were taken away. I only know that two people in uniforms showed up. It was dark. They had a helmet and each prisoner had to turn in everything they possessed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave Celebici camp finally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 31st August 1992 I was transferred to the sports hall in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the Commander of the Musala camp, the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, the sports hall was also under the command of Pavo Mucic, and his deputy, Hazim Delic, but Commander of the guard was Ismet Hebibovic, called Broceta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually have occasion to see either Mucic or Delic or Landzo in the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Mucic and Delic. I saw Delic more than Mucic but I saw Mucic when releasing some people from the sports hall and on that occasion, one day when people were being released, Hazim Delic personally beat me up in the sports hall. Later, in fact, maybe five or ten minutes before that, Pavo Mucic had left the sports hall and Zenga, that is Esad Landzo, occasionally dropped by the sports hall while I was there until 23rd December, but later was a guard again in the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were -- when were you released from any kind of detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was released on December 23rd from the sports hall at the initiative of the International Red Cross. I was released into home detention, when I was exchanged at the Butmir Airport in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have at this point, if your Honours remember, we filed an intention to show a video excerpt to Witness N if there are no objections from the defence lawyers, if the Chamber deems that appropriate. The excerpt video should be an excerpt deriving from seized material, seized videotapes which the prosecution is going to tender as exhibits in future through another witness who is an officer of the Austrian Police, who actually seized the videotapes. We pointed out in our request that there might be two possibilities for us to proceed to that. The first possibility is to call back the witness from where he lives after that the actual seized videotapes will be -- if they will be entered into evidence, and the other possibility is to have this excerpt shown to the witness today or tomorrow. Of course, then later if the tapes are admitted, the evidence may be considered. If the tapes are not admitted, then the court may strike or disregard the evidence. So if your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you are still hazy in your mind what you want to do and it is 5.30 now. You can think about it. We will know what to do tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. What has this witness to do with those excerpts?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will close until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The witness is in a position to recognise a number of people in those excerpt videos. (5.30 pm)
